newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH STATS BUREAU SAYS NO FORECAST RELEASED AUG 1.
newsitem.headline: CZECH STATS BUREAU SAYS NO FORECAST RELEASED AUG 1.

text.p: The official Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) will not compile an economic prognosis originally scheduled for August 1 since it published an extraordinary June outlook after the Czech crown's sharp fall, a spokesman said on Tuesday.

CSU spokesman Josef Zabransky said that the CSU may prepare another special update of its forecasts assessing the impact of July's flooding in the eastern part of the country, but no concrete plans have been made.
He said if a new prognosis would be done, it should be released by the beginning of October.

The CSU lowered its 1997 economic growth forecast in late June after speculative attacks on the crown caused the currency to fall more than 11 percent against its former mark/dollar basket when the central bank was forced to float it.

The CSU said in June that the economy would still get back on track after a sharp first quarter slowdown, with gross domestic product (GDP) expected to rise two to three percent this year after 4.1 percent real growth in 1996.
The forecast was lowered from CSU's May forecast of 2.9-3.5 percent growth, after GDP growth slowed to 1.5 percent in the first quarter from 4.6 in the same period last year.
